selection_reason: Gradient Boosting Regressor selected. The best non-tree candidate (Multi-Layer Perceptron Regressor) was ahead by only -0.0156 R-squared, inside the 0.02 margin, so the exact-SHAP-explainable model is preferred -- explainability is a stated requirement and the accuracy difference does not pay for losing it.

conformal.note: Coverage is with respect to the label the model was trained on. On the synthetic corpus that label is the generator's formula plus injected noise; the interval quantifies model error against that label and is not validation against real welfare outcomes.

candidates.name: linear_regression
candidates.rationale: Baseline. Establishes whether the signal-to-risk relationship is even roughly linear, and therefore whether any non-linear model in this comparison is earning its added complexity.

candidates.name: ridge_regression
candidates.rationale: Regularised linear variant. The behavioral signals are correlated by construction, which destabilises OLS coefficients; ridge is the standard remedy and is nearly free to include.

candidates.name: lasso_regression
candidates.rationale: Sparse linear variant. Zeroing a coefficient outright answers whether every behavioral signal is actually needed -- useful regardless of which model wins, since each signal has a data-collection cost.

candidates.name: random_forest
candidates.rationale: Bagged trees. Captures signal interactions without being told about them, which suits an interactive phenomenon, and supports an exact tree-based SHAP explanation.

candidates.name: gradient_boosting
candidates.rationale: Sequentially boosted trees, usually the strongest family on tabular data of this shape, and tree-based so explainability costs nothing.

candidates.name: hist_gradient_boosting
candidates.rationale: Histogram-binned boosting -- scikit-learn's equivalent of the LightGBM family, which is not installable here. Keeps that algorithm family in the comparison, and handles NaN natively.

candidates.name: support_vector_regression
candidates.rationale: Kernel method. Included for completeness even though it is unlikely to win: it fits a different kind of surface, so its result is informative either way.

candidates.name: mlp_regressor
candidates.rationale: Neural reference point. Answers whether the pattern needs a network at all, with a measurement rather than an assertion.
